paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to hold onto. In this chapter, one king looks like the most powerful man around, and one prisoner looks like he has nothing. Herod has the sword, the soldiers and the crowd cheering him on. But Peter sleeps between two soldiers, and the church is praying: "the church was fervently praying to God for him" (Acts 12:5).

Now look at who ends up where. Peter's chains fall off, and an iron gate opens by itself (Acts 12:7, 12:10). Herod puts on his royal robes, the people shout, "This is the voice of a god, not a man!" and then he is struck down because he "did not give glory to God" (Acts 12:22-23). The lesson is that God is the only one who is truly in charge, and every throne on earth is a borrowed seat. I think that's good news for you, because the things that look huge in your life are not bigger than Him.

And friend, notice what the praying people did when the answer showed up. They were so surprised they told Rhoda she was out of her mind (Acts 12:15)! I think that's the most comforting part, because God answered people who still had a little trouble believing it. Keep praying, keep trusting Him, and know that "the word of God continued to spread and multiply" (Acts 12:24). That doesn't depend on how steady your faith feels today, because it depends on Him.
